findings.title: Embedded-post username color lightness swapped
findings.body: The embedded post username link was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme branch is no longer 30% and the dark branch is the inverse of the usual 100-minus mapping. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness on `$primary` and puts `100 - N` on `$secondary`. Light themes will render these names much paler (weaker contrast); dark themes will not get the intended muted secondary color.

findings.title: Mobile flag length hint color inverted
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in this same PR correctly keeps 70% on `$primary` and uses 30% on `$secondary`. On mobile light themes the hint becomes much darker than before; on dark themes it is lightened far more than the desktop rule, so the two layouts no longer match and contrast with the modal background changes.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lightness changed
findings.body: `.topic-map h3` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop topic-map heading in this PR correctly becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`. Mobile light themes lose the stronger 20% color, and dark themes do not get the corresponding 80% secondary, so the heading is both a light-theme regression and inconsistent with desktop.

findings.title: Group member name color flattened to 50%
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The adjacent `.title` rule was already 50% and was converted correctly; the name rule was overwritten with that same 50/50 pair instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Light-theme group member names become lighter than before and no longer differ from titles.

findings.title: Mobile group member name color flattened to 50%
findings.body: The same mistake as desktop: `.group-member-info .name` changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, matching the sibling title instead of preserving 30% on `$primary` and using 70% on `$secondary`. Mobile light themes lose the darker name color, and dark themes do not follow the inversion used everywhere else in the PR.
